fits.fact: One Vietnamese seller names aquarium lights and air pumps as typical things to run on this strip.

For planted tanks, a smart-plug guide suggests putting the light, CO2 solenoid, air pump and optionally the heater on scheduled outlets. It treats the heater outlet only as a backup to the heater's own thermostat.
Total load has to stay within 2200W/10A, so check the strip's rating against large heaters or chillers before connecting them.
No source gives a water-resistance rating, so mount the strip away from splashes. None of these prices came from aquarium shops; they are from Vietnamese smart-home stores.

usage.fact: Pair it on a 2.4GHz network. Many home routers use 5GHz, and a separate 2.4GHz network for smart devices is suggested for reliability.
Name each outlet by its job (light, CO2, heater, air pump) in the Tuya/Smart Life app.
In the power-on setting, choose 'Last State' rather than 'Always On'. Otherwise a short power cut can leave CO2 running overnight.
Example schedule: lights 13:00–21:00, CO2 one hour before lights on until one hour before lights off, and the air pump at night only.
Put the outlets into one scene so the devices switch together instead of drifting on separate timers.
If the strip drops off Wi-Fi it keeps its stored schedule for several days, and unplugging it and plugging it back in usually reconnects it.
Control can be shared with family members through the app, for example while you travel.

issues.fact: A reef hobbyist reported that Tuya strips came back after a power outage with every outlet off, which leaves equipment unpowered if nobody is home.
The same hobbyist said about 5 of roughly 30 Tuya devices failed within two years, and that Tuya devices rely on the cloud and app.
Some cheap smart plugs switch off when Wi-Fi drops, which could stop a filter or CO2 mid-cycle. Check how yours behaves before trusting it with a filter.
Listings differ between versions: USB count (2 vs 4), stated weight (200 g vs 300 g) and warranty length (3 or 6 months).

alternatives.why: A better-supported brand: 3 smart outlets, 2300W/10A, 1.5 m cord, works with Apple Home, and 24-month warranty at one Vietnamese seller. It costs more (about 845,000–900,000 ₫), and its USB ports are always on and can't be controlled from the app.
The cheaper option (about 144,000 ₫ each) if you only need to time one or two devices, such as the light and CO2.
A Zigbee version of the same 4-outlet strip, if you already have a Zigbee hub. Price reported at about 590,000 ₫ on tuya.vn, but that page could not be opened to confirm.
